title: Minimax Estimation of Instrumental-Variable Bound Endpoints under Holder Margin Conditions
banked_reason: D0.5.G rated the maximized paper subfield, with paper_score_ceiling 7.3 below the 7.4 field cutoff; salvageable=false and no improvement directive.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a polynomial-rate characterization, not an exact minimax rate: the upper bound is n^{-1/2}+n^{-r}, while the nonparametric converse loses (log n)^{-q}.

The achieving procedure requires exhaustive search over an exponentially large deterministic Hölder cover, so the package supplies statistical existence rather than a computationally usable estimator.

Several load-bearing classical leaf results, especially Hölder sup-norm entropy and polynomial-approximation facts, are stated without proofs and are not all connected to precise theorem-level citations, leaving the supporting evidence short of publication-grade reproducibility.
proof_attempt_summary: The D stage built and repeatedly audited a legal 16-response-type IV witness, a strict-margin scalar-mixture converse, a finite-net oracle upper bound, honest one-sided excess bounds, and finite-family adaptation. The final core proves the shared polynomial exponent and root-n elbow for both a stronger anchored-contrast class and the promised response-cell-Hölder corollary, with all mathematics and five citation checks passing. It stopped below the field floor because the converse retains a logarithmic loss, the estimator is computationally exhaustive, and several classical supporting leaves need publication-grade proofs or theorem-level citations.
tldr: For a randomized binary instrument with any fixed known overlapping propensity and an otherwise arbitrary covariate law, the main theorem treats the stronger ambient class \(\mathcal P_{\alpha,\beta}(e;H_\theta,C_m,\eta)\): only the seven lower-face contrasts relative to face \(1\) are Hölder-\(\beta\), whereas the common face level and the individual response cells may be merely measurable and may lie on the multinomial boundary. Its minimax root-MSE and honest outer one-sided positive-excess frontiers have polynomial order \(n^{-1/2}+n^{-\beta(1+\alpha)/\{(2+\alpha)\beta+d\}}\), with a logarithmic loss only in the proved lower sandwich, root-\(n\) boundary \(\alpha\beta=d\), and rate-preserving adaptation over every fixed finite family. The originally promised componentwise-response-cell-Hölder result follows as a genuine corollary from \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{cell}}_{\alpha,\beta}(e;H,C_m,\eta)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\alpha,\beta}(e;1+7H,C_m,\eta)\): it has the same polynomial exponent, elbow, honest frontier, and fixed-family adaptation, and its matching lower sandwich holds once \(C_m\geq80^\alpha\) and \(H\) exceeds the finite common componentwise Hölder radius of the explicit smooth hard witnesses. Neither response-cell positivity nor a covariate-density condition is imposed on the response-cell class; uniform response-cell interiority belongs only to the hard witnesses.
gap: The exact endpoint is an average of a pointwise maximum. Levis et al. identify it and give a margin-powered direct-estimator remainder, then explicitly leave Hölder-margin minimax characterization open. Classification theory has the candidate arbitrary-design exponent, but classification regret does not lower-bound estimation of the integrated scalar endpoint; current aggregated-bound papers establish regular asymptotics under first-stage rate assumptions rather than a uniform phase diagram. Honest one-sided validity is known, but its minimax expected positive excess is not.
fill: Prove an upper bound by finite Hölder-cover face selection and held-out score evaluation; prove a scalar lower bound through an explicit 16-response-type IV embedding and punctured-support moment-matched priors; transfer the ordered lower experiment to honest one-sided excess; and add a three-way-split fixed-family oracle theorem. State only polynomial optimality, with exact logarithms, unknown propensity, continuum adaptation, and computational tractability excluded.
